target_customer: Corporate trucking fleets and shippers with partly empty trucks
problem: Full truckload shippers ran trucks below capacity while LTL shippers needed space, wasting capacity and money.
business_model: Matching marketplace for freight capacity (commission or software fee, not stated)
product_category: Freight capacity pooling and logistics software

competitors.name: Transfix
competitors.what: Digital freight matching with owner-operators and small fleets
competitors.traction_then: Revenue approaching $1M monthly and 6,000 plus drivers as of the article

competitors.name: Convoy
competitors.what: Uber-style trucking app, backed by Jeff Bezos
competitors.traction_then: Operational in Washington state as of the article

competitors.name: Cargomatic
competitors.what: Freight matching app, half its business container drayage
competitors.traction_then: Tens of thousands of loads moved

technical_complexity.rationale: Load matching and route optimization for pooled freight is standard logistics optimization with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Value depends on a two-sided shipper network, but freight matching rivals were well funded and the product was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Uber Freight launched in 2017 and Convoy kept growing, per a 2018 FreightWaves summary found in search. Viaopt left no public trace.

market_need_then: Trucking capacity waste and digital freight matching attracted many startups; the 2015 TT article lists eight such firms and a 2018 FreightWaves piece says hundreds had tried.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand assets, press or community found; name resembles unrelated ViOptix and VIAOPTIC trademarks.

outcome_analysis: Viaopt pitched an Uber pool for corporate trucking fleets with a two person team and went Inactive per the YC directory. No shutdown announcement, press coverage or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. It entered a crowded digital freight market with well funded rivals, but that is context, not a sourced cause. The only funding found is a small database entry consistent with the standard YC deal.
notes: Cause of inactivity not public. The company has no working website (YC page lists none). Funding rests on a single database: CB Insights says $120K over 2 rounds with a seed dated 2018-03-19, while Bounce Watch dates them 2018-01-04 and 2018-03-20 and places the company in Turkey. The recorded amount is likely the standard YC deal. Competitor source is dated November 2015, over two years before the batch, and Uber Freight is not in it. Founder education and employers not found.
